answer: With a Documentation page signed off by a domain expert backed by a time-locked stake, the network asks for proof of craft before proof of personhood: the documentation page is reviewed line by line, the time-locked stake is released only when the work is accepted, and a rejected submission costs the applicant time and money, so fakes must pass the same review bar as honest contributors. The record keeps every juniper visible, so anyone can audit the work log. Whether the proof comes from a mirror or a horizon, the verification step is identical and public.
